title: Constant-time comparison
summary: An ordinary equality check leaks how much of a secret you guessed right. Measure the leak, then close it.

steps.title: Equality that leaks
body: `==` on strings, `SequenceEqual` and a hand-written loop all **stop at the first difference**. That is efficient, and it is a leak: comparing a guess that is right in its first 5 bytes takes a little longer than one that is wrong in byte 1.

An attacker who can time many requests (over a network, the noise averages out) recovers a MAC or API key **one byte at a time**: try all 256 values of byte 1, keep the slowest, move on. That is at most 256 × 32 = 8,192 guesses for a 32-byte tag instead of 2^256.
The trace counts how many bytes an early-exit comparison looks at for three guesses. The count is the leak.

steps.prompt: This early-exit comparison counts the bytes it examines. What does it print?
code: for (int i = 0; i < secret.Length; i++) { n++; if (guess[i] != secret[i]) return n; }
steps.explain: The work done tells the attacker how many leading bytes are right. Time is a side channel that reports exactly this number.

steps.title: FixedTimeEquals
body: The fix is to always look at **every** byte and combine the differences, so the time depends only on the length:
diff |= a[i] ^ b[i];       // stays 0 only if every byte matches
.NET ships it, written so the JIT cannot optimise it back into an early exit:
Lengths may differ quickly; lengths of tags are public anyway. Compare **bytes**, not hex strings (decode first), and use it for every secret-dependent check: MACs, tokens, API keys, password hashes.

steps.explain: XOR is 0 for equal bytes, and OR-ing keeps any 1 bit that ever appeared. No branch depends on the data.
Decoding hex first makes upper and lower case equal, as they should be. Different lengths are simply unequal. Comparing hex *strings* both leaks timing and wrongly rejects a tag in the other case.

steps.prompt: Which comparisons should be constant-time? Select all that apply.
options: Checking an HMAC tag on an incoming webhook
Checking a presented API key against the stored one
Checking whether a username exists in a public member list
steps.explain: Anything where the attacker supplies a guess at a secret. A public list holds no secret, so its comparison leaks nothing worth having.

steps.title: Write FixedTimeEquals yourself
prompt: Write `bool ConstantTimeEquals(byte[] a, byte[] b)` without any early `return` or `break` inside the loop: return `false` straight away only if the lengths differ, otherwise XOR every pair, OR it into an accumulator, and compare the accumulator with 0 at the end.
template: Dojo.Check("equal arrays", ConstantTimeEquals(new byte[] { 1, 2, 3 }, new byte[] { 1, 2, 3 }), "returned false");
Dojo.Check("differ in the last byte", !ConstantTimeEquals(new byte[] { 1, 2, 3 }, new byte[] { 1, 2, 4 }), "returned true");
Dojo.Check("differ in the first byte", !ConstantTimeEquals(new byte[] { 9, 2, 3 }, new byte[] { 1, 2, 3 }), "returned true");
Dojo.Check("different lengths", !ConstantTimeEquals(new byte[] { 1, 2 }, new byte[] { 1, 2, 3 }), "returned true");
Dojo.Check("two empty arrays", ConstantTimeEquals(Array.Empty<byte>(), Array.Empty<byte>()), "returned false");
Dojo.Check("bits that cancel in a sum still count", !ConstantTimeEquals(new byte[] { 1, 2 }, new byte[] { 2, 1 }), "returned true");

forbid.message: Does not call SequenceEqual or FixedTimeEquals

hints: The only early return is for different lengths.

steps.title: Fix the API key check
prompt: This middleware compares API keys with `==` on strings, which leaks timing. The server stores only the SHA-256 of each key (so a database leak does not leak keys).

Fix `bool IsValidKey(string presented, byte[] storedHash)`: hash the presented key's UTF-8 bytes and compare with `CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals`. Hashing first also makes both sides the same length, whatever the caller sends.
template: Dojo.Check("the right key is accepted", IsValidKey("sk_live_dojo_123", dojoStored), "rejected the right key");
Dojo.Check("a wrong key is rejected", !IsValidKey("sk_live_dojo_124", dojoStored), "accepted a wrong key");
Dojo.Check("an empty key is rejected", !IsValidKey("", dojoStored), "accepted an empty key");
hints: Keep the hash as bytes instead of turning it into hex.
